extracted.intended_audience: ACL Rolling Review authors and reviewers (NLP/ML paper submitters and peer reviewers)
extracted.subtask_description: Checklist items and reviewer-verifiable criteria authors must complete for NLP papers submitted to ACL Rolling Review; reviewers verify answers and use them to inform soundness, reproducibility, and ethics assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Checklist completion requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Every NLP paper submitted through ACL Rolling Review must complete this checklist; reviewers verify completion and assess each section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must answer all applicable items (typically Yes/No); reviewers check completion and accuracy. The checklist standardises what an NLP review must cover beyond the substantive content of the paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: A1. Limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Did you describe the limitations of your work?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should explicitly discuss limitations. Reviewers verify that a limitations section or equivalent text appears and reasonably characterises what the work does not cover or where it may fail.

rubrics_metrics.name: A2. Risks
rubrics_metrics.description: Did you discuss any potential risks of your work?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should identify potential harms, misuse, or societal risks arising from the work. Reviewers check for an explicit discussion of risk and assess its completeness relative to the work's scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: B1. Creator Attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Did you cite the creators of artifacts you used?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must provide citation/attribution for datasets, models, tools, and other artifacts. Reviewers verify that creators are cited where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: B2. License and Terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Did you discuss the license or terms for use and / or distribution of any artifacts?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should state licenses and any usage restrictions for datasets, models, or code. Reviewers check that licenses/terms are reported and considered in authors' use/distribution plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: B3. Intended Use Compatibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Did you discuss if your use of existing artifact(s) was consistent with their intended use?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should assess whether their usage aligns with artifact creators' stated intended uses. Reviewers verify the authors' assessment and flag mismatches or unsupported repurposing.

rubrics_metrics.name: B4. Privacy and Offensive Content
rubrics_metrics.description: Did you discuss the steps taken to check whether the data ... contains any information that names or uniquely identifies individual people or offensive content?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should describe checks for personally identifying information (PII) and offensive content, and mitigation steps taken. Reviewers verify that appropriate checks/mitigations are reported and adequate for the dataset's nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: B5. Artifact Documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Did you provide documentation of the artifacts, e.g., coverage of domains, languages, and linguistic phenomena?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should provide documentation describing artifact provenance, domains, languages, and relevant phenomena. Reviewers assess whether documentation is sufficient to understand artifact scope and limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: B6. Data Statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: Did you report relevant statistics like the number of examples, details of train / test / dev splits?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must report dataset sizes, splits, and other relevant descriptive statistics. Reviewers verify reported statistics and that they are sufficient to reproduce experiments and interpret results.

rubrics_metrics.name: C1. Model Parameters and Computational Budget
rubrics_metrics.description: Did you report the number of parameters in the models used, the total computational budget ... and computing infrastructure used?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should report model sizes, compute used for training/evaluation (e.g., FLOPs, GPU hours), and infrastructure details. Reviewers check completeness and plausibility of reported computational resource information.

rubrics_metrics.name: C2. Experimental Setup
rubrics_metrics.description: Did you discuss the experimental setup, including hyperparameter search and best-found hyperparameter values?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should describe experimental procedures, hyperparameter search strategy, and chosen hyperparameters. Reviewers verify that setup details allow reproducibility and that hyperparameter tuning is adequately reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: C3. Result Statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: Did you report descriptive statistics about your results (e.g., error bars around results)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should report variability measures (confidence intervals, standard deviations, multiple runs) and other descriptive statistics. Reviewers check for appropriate reporting of uncertainty and variability, not just single-point estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: C4. Package Implementation Details
rubrics_metrics.description: If you used existing packages ... did you report the implementation, model, and parameter settings used?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must state software packages, versions, model implementations, and parameter settings. Reviewers verify that implementation details are sufficient to reproduce results and disambiguate differences due to packages.

rubrics_metrics.name: D1. Participant Instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Did you report the full text of instructions given to participants?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For human-subjects work, authors should include verbatim instructions provided to participants (e.g., annotation guidelines, survey prompts). Reviewers ensure full instructions are reported and evaluate their clarity and appropriateness.

rubrics_metrics.name: D2. Recruitment and Payment
rubrics_metrics.description: Did you report information about how you recruited ... and paid participants?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should describe recruitment channels, inclusion/exclusion criteria, and compensation. Reviewers check that recruitment and payment are reported and ethically appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: D3. Consent
rubrics_metrics.description: Did you discuss whether and how consent was obtained from people whose data you're using?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must describe consent procedures for data subjects or participants (including opt-in/opt-out mechanisms). Reviewers verify consent reporting and adequacy for the data's use.

rubrics_metrics.name: D4. Ethics Board Approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Was the data collection protocol approved (or determined exempt) by an ethics review board?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should state IRB/ethics approval or exemption details for data collection. Reviewers check for documented ethics review status and escalate concerns if absent where required.

rubrics_metrics.name: D5. Annotator Demographics
rubrics_metrics.description: Did you report the basic demographic and geographic characteristics of the annotator population?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should report annotator demographics (age ranges, gender, geographic location, language background, etc.) insofar as ethical/privacy constraints allow. Reviewers assess whether demographic reporting is adequate to evaluate biases and generalisability.

rubrics_metrics.name: E1. AI Assistant Disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: If you used any AI assistants, did you include information about your use?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should disclose use of AI assistants (e.g., for writing, data analysis, generation) and describe provenance/roles. Reviewers verify that AI assistant usage is disclosed and described sufficiently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer obligation: verify author answers
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must check that author Yes/No answers to every applicable item are accurate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each checklist item authors mark, reviewers should confirm the paper contains the evidence supporting the answer. Inaccurate or unsupported Yes answers should be noted in the review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer obligation: flag No-without-justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must flag any No-without-justification as a concern (not necessarily a rejection ground).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If authors answer 'No' and do not provide justification or rationale, reviewers should highlight this as a concern for the area (e.g., missing documentation, missing consent). This informs but does not by itself require rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer obligation: inform Soundness/Reproducibility/Ethical Concerns scores
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must use the checklist completion to inform the Soundness, Reproducibility, and Ethical Concerns scores in the ARR review form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checklist responses should directly influence scoring of these review dimensions. Missing or inadequate checklist items should lower reproducibility/soundness/ethics assessments as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer obligation: ethics escalation for missing essential D items
rubrics_metrics.description: A paper failing essential D-section items (e.g. consent for human-subjects data) is a candidate for ethics escalation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If authors fail to meet critical human-subjects requirements (e.g., no consent, no ethics board review when required), reviewers should consider escalating to ethics chairs or follow the venue's escalation procedure.
